Definition: {properly, a region across; but used only adverbially (with or without a preposition) on the opposite side (especially of the Jordan; ususally meaning the east)}
BiblicalUsage: In Aramaic this word means ‘beyond’ or ‘the other side’ — almost always ‘beyond the river’, the Euphrates, the boundary of the Persian province. The accusers warn about the lands ‘beyond the river’; and Darius orders the governor ‘beyond the river’ to leave the builders alone.
TheologicalSignificance: It is a boundary word, and it marks where one power ends and another begins — but in Ezra the real boundary is God’s, and no governor beyond the river can stop what He has decreed.
